16	- main page: a terminal-styled web view over a Claude Code session (primary UI)

26	## What already exists in `.claude/` (and why it matters)
27	
28	`.claude/shared/monitoring/` is a working, dependency-free (bash + Python 3
29	stdlib + browser) implementation of live orchestrator monitoring — effectively a
30	prior-art prototype of Touch's visual half. Full reference:
31	`.claude/shared/monitoring/monitoring.md`.

34	
35	```
36	agents ──status.sh──┐
37	                    ├──> <task-dir>/events.jsonl ──> monitor_server.py ──ws──> monitor.html
38	Workflow journal ───┘        (append-only,          (HTTP + WebSocket)
39	  via decision_watcher.py     single source of truth)
40	```
41	
42	- `status.sh <plan> <stage> <state> [detail]` — appends one JSON event line.
43	  Requires `ORCH_STATE_DIR`; falls back to the module dir with a stderr warning.
44	- `decision_watcher.py` — tails a Workflow run's `journal.jsonl`, derives
45	  spawn/verdict/retry/advance events and per-agent token accounting from the
46	  `[monitor] plan=… stage=… role=… attempt=…` marker embedded in every agent
47	  prompt. This marker is the **deterministic** event source — it works with zero
48	  LLM cooperation; `status.sh` calls inside agents are best-effort color only.
49	  Checkpointed in `.watcher-state.json` (restart-safe, never double-counts).
50	- `monitor_server.py` — serves `monitor.html` at `/`, streams events at `/ws`
51	  (full replay on connect, then live tail, `?task=<name>`), plus `/tasks`,
52	  `/artifacts?task=`, `/file?task=&path=` (extension-whitelisted, realpath
53	  contained), `/health`. One server serves all tasks; one watcher per task.
54	- Event schema, reserved ids (`plan` id `orchestrator`; stages `plan`,
55	  `complete`, `tokens`), and token-delta semantics are specified in
56	  `monitoring.md` — treat that file as normative.
57	
58	State layout: the module is **stateless and task-agnostic** — never copy or
59	modify it per task. Per-run state lives in
60	`.claude/local-orchestrators/<task-name>/` (`events.jsonl`, `orch-config.json`,
61	`.watcher-state.json`, `orch-scripts/`, `findings/`, `plan/`, `report/`).

64	
65	`execute-research` → ONE complete plan file → `implement-plan` → implementation.
66	
67	- `execute-research`: parallel read-only researchers (one per perspective,
68	  `opus`) with a barrier, then ONE `fable` synthesizer that writes
69	  `plan/<name>-plan.md` (global decisions + ordered items). Never partitions,
70	  never edits source.
71	- `implement-plan`: a `fable` divider derives isolated sub-plans by **file
72	  ownership** (one file, exactly one owner), then per sub-plan runs a gated
73	  loop — brand-new implementer each attempt → read-only test gate → read-only
74	  adversarial critique — until green or MAX_ATTEMPTS, then a final aggregate
75	  gate over the merged change-set. **Serial by default**; parallel only when
76	  explicitly asked and only for disjoint file ownership.
77	- Both skills' `templates/*.workflow.js` are the **normative protocol** (prompts,
78	  schemas, models, markers, status calls). Adapt a copy into the task folder's
79	  `orch-scripts/`; don't diverge from the invariants.
80	- Handoff between attempts is via `findings/<plan>-<gate>-attempt-<N>.md` file
81	  paths, not inlined text.
82	- Never resume/continue/`SendMessage` a prior agent — always a fresh subagent.
83

1	# Orchestrator monitoring module
2	
3	Reusable, task-agnostic live monitoring for deterministic orchestrator runs
4	(Workflow-tool scripts, or any driver that spawns agents). This module lives
5	in `.claude/shared/monitoring/` and is stateless; each task keeps its
6	orchestration scripts and monitoring state (events, config, checkpoints) in
7	`.claude/local-orchestrators/<task-name>/`, selected via the
8	`ORCH_STATE_DIR` env var. See the `m-orchestrator` skill for the
9	integration checklist.
10	
11	Zero third-party dependencies: bash + Python 3 stdlib + a browser.
12	
13	## Files
14	
15	| File | Role |
16	|------|------|
17	| `status.sh` | Deterministic trace point — agents/orchestrators append status events |
18	| `events.jsonl` | Append-only event stream (single source of truth; created on first event) |
19	| `monitor_server.py` | HTTP + WebSocket server: serves `monitor.html` at `/`, streams `events.jsonl` at `/ws` (full replay on connect, then live tail; `?task=<name>` selects a task), `/tasks` lists every discovered task folder, `/artifacts?task=<name>` lists the task's `.html`/`.md` artifacts, `/file?task=<name>&path=<rel>` serves one (extension-whitelisted, realpath-contained), `/health` probe |
20	| `monitor.html` | Live dashboard — one card per plan, event-driven, no rebuild for updates; header dropdown switches between running tasks live; task page shows an artifacts strip (final HTML report opens in a new tab, `.md` notes open an in-page preview) |
21	| `decision_watcher.py` | Tails a Workflow run's `journal.jsonl`; emits orchestrator decision events + per-agent token accounting into `events.jsonl` |
22	| `orch-config.json` | Optional config: `wf_dir` (workflow transcript dir), `port`, and attempt caps `max_plan_attempts` (default 4) / `max_gate_attempts` (default 3) / `max_e2e_attempts` (default 3) that the decision watcher reads for its retry/exhausted decision narration |
23	| `.watcher-state.json` | Watcher checkpoint (journal offset, agent classifications, token baselines) — restart-safe, never duplicates events |
24	
25	## Event schema
26	
27	One JSON object per line in `events.jsonl`:
28	
29	```json
30	{"ts": "<ISO-8601>", "plan": "<plan-id>", "stage": "<stage>", "state": "queued|running|done|failed|info|stale", "detail": "<short text>", "title": "<optional card title>", "tokens": {"in": 0, "out": 0, "cached": 0, "cache_write": 0}, "quiet": true}
31	```
32	
33	The decision watcher additionally attaches a per-subagent `agent` sub-object to
34	its events; it drives the live per-agent rows and the impl→test→critique flow
35	strip on the plan card:
36	
37	```json
38	{"agent": {"id": "<agent-id>", "label": "<short label>", "state": "running|done|failed|stale", "tokens": {"in": 0, "out": 0, "cached": 0, "cache_write": 0}, "started": "<ISO-8601>", "runtime": "<seconds or human string>"}}
39	```
40	
41	- `plan` — one card per unique id, first-seen order. **Reserved id `orchestrator`**: rendered as a wide card pinned last; the decision watcher writes there.
42	- `stage` — free-form; each unique stage gets a colored chip on the card. **Reserved stages**: `plan` (sets the card's badge to `state` — use for plan lifecycle: queued/running/done/failed), `complete` (alias of `plan` for badge purposes — use for the final run-summary event on the `orchestrator` card), `tokens` (updates the card's token counter; no chip).
43	- `title` — optional on any event; renames the card (or set `ORCH_TITLE` env with `status.sh`).
44	- `tokens` — **delta** (not absolute) added to the card's counter; grand total is derived by the page. `in` is TOTAL input (fresh + cache writes + cache reads); optional `cached` is the cache-read (`r:`) portion and optional `cache_write` is the cache-write (`w:`) portion, letting the page display the fresh input plus an `r:`/`w:` cache breakdown (an agent loop re-reads its whole prefix every turn, so cache reads dominate `in`). Events without `cached`/`cache_write` render as plain `in`.
45	- `agent` — optional per-subagent sub-object (watcher-emitted; see the block above) with the agent's `id`/`label`, its own `state` (`running|done|failed|stale`), a nested `tokens` breakdown, and `started`/`runtime`.
46	- `quiet` — update counters only, no log line (used for ~1s live token ticks).
47	
48	## Plugging into a new orchestration
49	
50	1. **Seed cards** (optional but recommended) before launching:
51	   ```bash
52	   ORCH_TITLE="Phase 1 — parser" ./status.sh phase1 plan queued "short description"
53	   ```
54	2. **Embed the classification marker** in every agent prompt so the decision
55	   watcher needs no task-specific patterns:
56	   ```
57	   [monitor] plan=<plan-id> stage=<stage> role=<role> attempt=<n>
58	   ```
59	   (`stage=` is optional; without it the watcher derives the stage from the
60	   mandated `status.sh ... running` command text in the prompt. If the
61	   prompt embeds quoted text containing stray markers — e.g. findings JSON
62	   from an earlier agent — the LAST occurrence wins, since the orchestrator
63	   script appends its marker at the end.)
64	
65	   **This marker is the deterministic event source.** The prompt text is
66	   authored by the orchestrator script at a fixed control-flow point and is
67	   recorded in the Workflow journal; the watcher raises `running` (on spawn)
68	   and `done`/`failed`/`info` (on result, derived from the structured-output
69	   shape: `findings`/`real`/`fixed_ids`/`files_changed`/`passed`/`approved`)
70	   events onto the
71	   plan's card, plus plan-badge transitions (first spawn → `running`,
72	   decisive green result → `done`, a new sequenced plan starting → closes
73	   the prior one). A decisive close is provisional: if a later agent spawns
74	   for the same plan (multi-gate loops — e.g. test green while e2e/critique
75	   still follow), the watcher reopens the card with a
76	   `plan running "loop continues: ..."` event; the badge that survives with
77	   no further spawns is the true close. None of this depends on the agent
78	   LLM doing anything.
79	
80	   Two robustness rules cover harness gaps. (1) `stale` rows: an agent whose
81	   journal `started` never gets a `result` (driver killed/restarted) is
82	   closed as `stale` when the same plan+role respawns — its runtime is its
83	   last transcript activity; the dashboard also freezes any still-"running"
84	   rows as `stale` when their plan card closes. (2) Completion time: journal
85	   entries carry no timestamps and a transcript can stop flushing mid-run
86	   (a long final Bash call), so when tailing live the watcher stamps results
87	   with the read moment unless the transcript's last line is fresh (≤30s).
88	
89	   Roles `impl`, `test`, `critique`, `gate:run`, `gate:fix`, `e2e:run`,
90	   `e2e:fix` get semantic decision lines (approve/reject/retry/advance);
91	   any other role gets a generic "finished" line. Token accounting works for
92	   every role.
93	3. **Optionally mandate trace calls in agent prompts** for intra-agent
94	   detail (progress notes between spawn and result — the only thing the
95	   journal cannot see):
96	   ```
97	   FIRST run: bash <abs-path>/status.sh <plan> <stage> running "attempt N: ..."
98	   LAST  run: bash <abs-path>/status.sh <plan> <stage> done|failed "attempt N: <summary>"
99	   ```
100	   These are best-effort color on top of the deterministic stream — an agent
101	   that skips them costs nothing but its own extra detail lines.
102	
103	   **When the whole run ends, the driver SHOULD emit a final badge event for
104	   the orchestrator card** with the run summary and token totals only the
105	   driver knows:
106	   ```bash
107	   ./status.sh orchestrator complete done "wf_<id> complete: <summary>"
108	   ```
109	   The watcher also closes the badge on its own (safety net): once every
110	   tracked agent has a result, every plan's loop is closed, and the journal
111	   stays quiet for `ORCH_QUIET_SECS` (default 60s), it emits
112	   `orchestrator complete done|failed` itself — so a driver that loses its
113	   context mid-run (`/clear`, compaction, killed session) no longer leaves
114	   the card `running` forever. A premature watcher close (unusually long
115	   pause between loops) self-heals: the next spawn reopens the badge with
116	   `complete running`.
117	4. **Start the daemons** (any order; both resolve paths relative to their own
118	   location, so run them from anywhere):
119	   ```bash
120	   ORCH_STATE_DIR=<task-dir> python3 monitor_server.py &    # port: argv > $ORCH_PORT > config > 8931
121	   ORCH_STATE_DIR=<task-dir> python3 decision_watcher.py &  # wf_dir: argv > $ORCH_WF_DIR > config > newest wf_* journal
122	   ```
123	   The watcher survives `/clear` / `/compact` in the driver session: those
124	   rotate the session id, which relocates where the harness writes subagent
125	   transcripts mid-run (`.../<new-session>/subagents/workflows/<wf>/`). The
126	   journal stays at its launch-time path, and the watcher searches every
127	   session dir holding the same `<wf>` name for per-agent transcripts,
128	   deduping token counts by API message id — so classification, live tokens,
129	   and runtimes keep working across rotations.
130	   `ORCH_STATE_DIR` selects the task state folder (events.jsonl, config,
131	   checkpoint); unset, state lands next to the scripts.
132	   The watcher auto-discovers the most recently active
133	   `~/.claude/projects/*/*/subagents/workflows/wf_*/journal.jsonl` when not
134	   configured — set `wf_dir` in `orch-config.json` to pin a specific run.
135	5. **Open the dashboard**: `http://<host>:8931/`. In a sandbox whose ports the
136	   host can't reach, run `monitor_server.py` on the host instead — if this
137	   folder is on a shared mount, it tails the same `events.jsonl` the sandboxed
138	   agents write.
139	
140	   One `monitor_server.py` serves every task: it rescans
141	   `.claude/local-orchestrators/*/` on each request (`/tasks` endpoint), and
142	   the dashboard's header dropdown switches the live stream between them —
143	   no restart needed when a new orchestration starts. `ORCH_STATE_DIR` only
144	   picks which task is selected by default. `decision_watcher.py` still
145	   watches one task per process — start one per concurrent orchestration.
146	
147	## Task-page artifacts (final report + agent notes)
148	
149	The task page shows an **artifacts row** inside the cards grid — after the
150	plan/loop cards and before the wide Orchestrator card — refreshed every 5s
151	from `/artifacts?task=<name>`:
152	
153	- **`.html`/`.htm` files** (e.g. the final illustrated report the driver
154	  writes when the run completes) render as a highlighted link that opens the
155	  report in a new tab. Reports are served with `Content-Security-Policy:
156	  sandbox allow-scripts`, so a self-contained report (inline CSS/JS) renders
157	  fully but its scripts run in an opaque origin, cut off from the monitor.
158	- **`.md` files** (gate findings, reviews/critiques, research notes, plans —
159	  anything agents persist for other agents) render as chips that open an
160	  in-page preview modal (escape-first mini markdown renderer: headings,
161	  lists, fenced code, tables, blockquotes; "open raw" links the plain text).
162	
163	Discovery is convention-free: every non-hidden `.html`/`.md` under the task
164	folder (depth ≤ 3 of subdirectories, e.g. `findings/`, `reviews/`, `plan/`,
165	`report/`) is listed, reports first. So the only requirement on drivers and
166	gate prompts is the existing one — **write handoff notes and the final report
167	into the task state folder** — and they appear on the dashboard
168	automatically. `/file` never serves other extensions, hidden entries, or any
169	path resolving outside the task folder (traversal/symlink safe).
170	
171	## Behavior notes
172	
173	- **Full replay on connect**: the page resets and rebuilds on every
174	  (re)connect — safe against double counting; token-counter pulse animations
175	  are suppressed during the replay burst and only fire on live changes.
176	- **Timestamps are true occurrence times** where derivable: the watcher stamps
177	  spawn events from the agent transcript's first line and results from its
178	  last line; live events lag ≤1s (poll interval). Rendered in viewer-local time.
179	- **Token math**: per-agent usage is summed from transcript `message.usage`,
180	  deduplicated by API message id; input includes cache creation + cache reads.
181	  All emitted `tokens` values are deltas against the watcher's checkpoint, so
182	  restarts and live ticks never double-count.
183	- **Completed tasks are history — never delete them.** When a run finishes
184	  (all plans done), leave the task folder and its `events.jsonl` in place.
185	  The monitor lists every surviving folder in `/tasks` and replays the full
186	  event history on connect, so a freshly started `monitor_server.py` shows
187	  old runs' complete progress — that only works if the events survive.
188	- **Resetting a run** (wipe-and-rerun of ONE task you are still iterating on
189	  — never post-completion cleanup): stop the daemons, delete that task's
190	  `events.jsonl` and `.watcher-state.json`, re-seed, restart. The watcher
191	  will re-backfill the whole journal with true timestamps.
192	- **Do not `pkill -f` these scripts from a command line that also spells the
193	  script name** — bracket the first letter (`pkill -f "[m]onitor_server"`).
194	- **State-dir authority — always set `ORCH_STATE_DIR`.** The shared module
195	  directory (`.claude/shared/monitoring/`) is code-only and is NOT an
196	  authoritative state dir. `status.sh` falls back to it (and warns on stderr)
197	  when `ORCH_STATE_DIR` is unset, so a forgotten variable dribbles a stray
198	  `events.jsonl` into the module dir; the daemons no longer short-circuit onto
199	  that file, and `.claude/shared/monitoring/events.jsonl` /
200	  `.watcher-state.json` are gitignored — but every `status.sh` call should still
201	  set `ORCH_STATE_DIR` to the task folder so events land where the daemons watch.
202

79	    try:
80	        st = os.stat(events_path)
81	    except OSError:
82	        return {"status": "empty", "last": None, "tokens": {"in": 0, "out": 0}}
83	    key = (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size)

114	    if orch in ("done", "failed"):

266	    header = bytearray([0x80 | opcode])

279	def parse_client_frames(buf: bytearray) -> bool:
280	    """Consume whole client->server frames from ``buf`` in place.
281	
282	    Returns True if a CLOSE frame (opcode 0x8) was seen. Client frames are
283	    always masked (RFC 6455); we only need enough parsing to detect CLOSE and
284	    to skip over pong/other frames so a following CLOSE in the same read is not
285	    missed. Incomplete trailing bytes are left in ``buf`` for the next read.
286	    """
287	    saw_close = False
288	    while len(buf) >= 2:
289	        opcode = buf[0] & 0x0F
290	        masked = buf[1] & 0x80
291	        length = buf[1] & 0x7F
292	        idx = 2
293	        if length == 126:
294	            if len(buf) < idx + 2:
295	                break
296	            length = int.from_bytes(buf[idx:idx + 2], "big")
297	            idx += 2
298	        elif length == 127:
299	            if len(buf) < idx + 8:
300	                break
301	            length = int.from_bytes(buf[idx:idx + 8], "big")
302	            idx += 8
303	        if masked:
304	            idx += 4  # 4-byte masking key
305	        if len(buf) < idx + length:
306	            break  # frame body not fully arrived yet
307	        del buf[:idx + length]
308	        if opcode == 0x8:
309	            saw_close = True
310	    return saw_close

314	    """Discard incoming frames (pongs); flag close on CLOSE frame/EOF so the writer stops."""
315	    buf = bytearray()

317	        while True:
318	            data = await reader.read(4096)
319	            if not data:

330	def read_frames(events_path: str, offset: int):
331	    """Read complete newline-terminated records appended since ``offset``.
332	
333	    Returns ``(frames, new_offset)`` where ``frames`` is the list of stripped
334	    non-empty lines up to the last ``\\n`` and ``new_offset`` advances by exactly
335	    those bytes, leaving any incomplete trailing line for the next tick (D5).
336	    A negative sentinel offset of ``-1`` signals truncation (``size < offset``);
337	    the caller closes the stream so the client reconnects cleanly (D10).
338	    """
339	    try:
340	        size = os.path.getsize(events_path)
341	    except OSError:
342	        return [], offset
343	    if size < offset:  # truncated/rotated under a live socket
344	        return [], -1
345	    if size <= offset:
346	        return [], offset
347	    with open(events_path, "rb") as f:
348	        f.seek(offset)
349	        data = f.read()
350	    nl = data.rfind(b"\n")
351	    if nl == -1:
352	        return [], offset  # no complete line yet; defer the partial tail
353	    complete = data[:nl + 1]
354	    frames = [line for line in (ln.strip() for ln in complete.splitlines()) if line]
355	    return frames, offset + len(complete)

154	def agent_tokens(agent_id: str) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
155	    """Sum (input, cache-read, cache-write, output) tokens across an agent's API calls, deduped by message id.
156	
157	    ``input`` is the TOTAL input volume (fresh + cache writes + cache reads).
158	    Cache reads/writes are broken out separately because an agent loop
159	    re-sends its whole conversation prefix every turn — cache reads dominate
160	    the input sum (and cost ~10x less than fresh input), so displays show
161	    the r:/w: breakdown to keep the big number interpretable.
162	    """
163	    # A /clear- or /compact-split transcript yields several copies; the
164	    # message-id key unions them safely (overlapping messages collapse).
165	    usage_by_msg: dict[str, dict] = {}
166	    for path in agent_paths(agent_id):
167	        try:
168	            with open(path) as f:
169	                for lineno, raw in enumerate(f):
170	                    try:
171	                        d = json.loads(raw)
172	                    except json.JSONDecodeError:
173	                        continue
174	                    if d.get("type") != "assistant":
175	                        continue
176	                    m = d.get("message") or {}
177	                    u = m.get("usage")
178	                    if u:
179	                        # Fall back to a stable per-row key (path+line) when the
180	                        # entry carries neither message.id nor uuid, so multiple
181	                        # id-less usage rows are summed rather than collapsing to
182	                        # a single "" key (WATCHER-8).
183	                        key = m.get("id") or d.get("uuid")
184	                        if not key:
185	                            key = f"\0noid\0{path}\0{lineno}"
186	                        usage_by_msg[key] = u
187	        except OSError:
188	            continue
189	    tin = tcached = twrite = tout = 0
190	    for u in usage_by_msg.values():
191	        cached = u.get("cache_read_input_tokens") or 0
192	        write = u.get("cache_creation_input_tokens") or 0
193	        tin += (u.get("input_tokens") or 0) + write + cached
194	        tcached += cached
195	        twrite += write
196	        tout += u.get("output_tokens") or 0
197	    return tin, tcached, twrite, tout

258	def _last_ts_in_file(path: str) -> str | None:
259	    """Latest parseable ``timestamp`` in one transcript file.
260	
261	    Grows the tail window until at least one full line is captured, so a final
262	    transcript line larger than the initial window (a >64KB tool result — the
263	    real case commit 0586bbbf shows) still yields the true last timestamp
264	    instead of an older one or ``None`` (WATCHER-7).
265	    """
266	    try:
267	        size = os.path.getsize(path)
268	    except OSError:
269	        return None
270	    window = 65536
271	    while True:
272	        start = max(0, size - window)
273	        try:
274	            with open(path, "rb") as f:
275	                f.seek(start)
276	                data = f.read()
277	        except OSError:
278	            return None
279	        if start > 0:
280	            # Drop the leading (probably partial) line we started mid-way into.
281	            nl = data.find(b"\n")
282	            data = data[nl + 1:] if nl != -1 else b""
283	        for line in reversed(data.decode(errors="replace").splitlines()):
284	            try:
285	                ts = json.loads(line).get("timestamp")
286	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
287	                continue
288	            if ts:
289	                return ts
290	        if start == 0:  # whole file scanned, still nothing parseable
291	            return None
292	        window *= 2

305	def result_ts(agent_id: str, live: bool) -> str | None:
306	    """Completion timestamp for an agent whose journal ``result`` just landed.
307	
308	    Journal entries carry no timestamps, and a transcript can stop flushing
309	    mid-run — a long final Bash call leaves the tool result and everything
310	    after it unwritten, so the transcript's last line may predate the real
311	    finish by many minutes. When tailing live (the entry appeared since the
312	    previous ~1s poll) the read moment IS the completion time; trust the
313	    transcript timestamp only when it is fresh enough to be the real end.
314	    On backlog catch-up the transcript is the only signal we have.
315	    """
316	    t_tr = last_ts(agent_id)
317	    if not live:
318	        return t_tr
319	    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
320	    if t_tr:
321	        try:
322	            parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(t_tr.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
323	            if (now - parsed).total_seconds() <= 30:
324	                return t_tr
325	        except ValueError:
326	            pass
327	    return now.isoformat(timespec="milliseconds")

330	def classify(agent_id: str, retries: int = 3) -> dict | None:
331	    # Runs inline in the single ~1s poll thread, so the total wait per call is
332	    # kept small (a few 0.5s retries at most): a transcript that hasn't flushed
333	    # yet falls through to "pending" (returns None) rather than stalling the
334	    # loop for seconds while live token ticks and run-completion go unserved
335	    # (WATCHER-5). The caller re-attempts classification on the later result
336	    # entry, by which point the transcript is written.
337	    for _ in range(retries):
338	        text = prompt_text(agent_id)
339	        if text:
340	            # Last occurrence wins: the orchestrator script appends its marker at
341	            # the end of the prompt, and earlier text may embed quoted findings
342	            # that leaked a previous agent's marker.
343	            m = None
344	            for m in MARKER.finditer(text):
345	                pass
346	            if m:
347	                stage = m.group(2)
348	                if not stage:
349	                    sh = None
350	                    for sh in STAGE_HINT.finditer(text):
351	                        pass
352	                    stage = sh.group(1) if sh else None
353	                role = m.group(3)
354	                return {"plan": m.group(1), "role": role, "attempt": int(m.group(4)),
355	                        "stage": stage or role.split(":")[-1]}
356	            for pattern, role in ROLE_PATTERNS:
357	                m = pattern.search(text)
358	                if m:
359	                    if role in ("impl", "test", "critique"):
360	                        return {"plan": m.group(1), "role": role, "attempt": int(m.group(2)),
361	                                "stage": role}
362	                    plan = role.split(":")[0]
363	                    return {"plan": plan, "role": role, "attempt": int(m.group(1)),
364	                            "stage": role.split(":")[-1]}
365	            return None
366	        time.sleep(0.5)
367	    return None

370	def describe_result(info: dict, result) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
371	    """Return (stage, state, detail) decision line for a finished agent.
372	
373	    Shape-driven: keyed on the structured-output fields the orchestrator
374	    script's schemas force, so the line reflects the actual returned data.
375	    """
376	    plan, role, attempt = info["plan"], info["role"], info["attempt"]
377	    stage = plan
378	    if result is None:
379	        return stage, "failed", f"{plan} {role} #{attempt} died or was skipped"
380	    r = result if isinstance(result, dict) else {}
381	    if role == "impl" and ("files_changed" in r or "changed_files" in r):
382	        # Canonical impl key is files_changed (D1); tolerate the legacy alias.
383	        files = r.get("files_changed", r.get("changed_files")) or []
384	        return stage, "info", f"{plan} impl #{attempt} returned {len(files)} changed files -> spawn test"
385	    if role == "test" and "passed" in r:
386	        if r["passed"]:
387	            return stage, "done", f"{plan} test #{attempt} PASS -> spawn critique"
388	        return stage, "failed", f"{plan} test #{attempt} FAIL -> critique will reject; feedback loops"
389	    if "approved" in r:
390	        if r["approved"]:
391	            return stage, "done", f"decision: {plan} approved on attempt {attempt} -> plan complete"
392	        nxt = (f"retry attempt {attempt + 1}/{MAX_PLAN_ATTEMPTS}"
393	               if attempt < MAX_PLAN_ATTEMPTS else "attempts exhausted -> plan FAILED")
394	        return stage, "failed", f"decision: {plan} attempt {attempt} rejected -> {nxt}"
395	    if "findings" in r:
396	        return stage, "info", f"{plan} {role} #{attempt}: {len(r['findings'])} findings"
397	    if "real" in r:
398	        return stage, "info", f"{plan} verify #{attempt}: real={r['real']}"
399	    if "fixed_ids" in r:
400	        return stage, "info", (f"{plan} {role} #{attempt}: fixed {len(r.get('fixed_ids') or [])}, "
401	                               f"skipped {len(r.get('skipped_ids') or [])}")
402	    if "passed" in r:
403	        ok = r["passed"]
404	        loop = "gate" if ("gate" in role or plan in ("fullsuite", "gate")) else "e2e"
405	        cap = MAX_GATE_ATTEMPTS if loop == "gate" else MAX_E2E_ATTEMPTS
406	        # stage stays the plan name: the spawn event opened the chip under
407	        # `plan`, and a result under any other stage would orphan it as
408	        # "running" forever; the loop identity lives in the detail text.
409	        if ok:
410	            advance = "advance" if loop == "gate" else "workflow COMPLETE"
411	            return stage, "done", f"decision: {plan} {loop} attempt {attempt} green -> {advance}"
412	        nxt = (f"spawn fixer, then retry {attempt + 1}/{cap}"
413	               if attempt < cap else f"{loop} attempts exhausted -> FAILED")
414	        return stage, "failed", f"decision: {plan} {loop} attempt {attempt} failed -> {nxt}"
415	    return stage, "info", f"{plan} {role} #{attempt} finished"

450	def run_outcome(state: dict) -> str | None:
451	    """Terminal run state implied by the journal so far, or None while live.
452	
453	    "done" when every plan's loop closed green; "failed" when every signal
454	    left is a rejection (attempts exhausted). The caller still debounces:
455	    a rejection about to retry, or a pause between loops, looks terminal for
456	    a moment — and any later spawn reopens the badge, so a premature close
457	    self-heals (same contract as the per-plan reopen logic below).
458	    """
459	    if not state["plans"] or state["running"]:
460	        return None
461	    still_open = [p for p, v in state["plans"].items() if v not in ("done", "failed")]
462	    if still_open and not all(state["decisive"].get(p) is False for p in still_open):
463	        return None
464	    ok = (not still_open
465	          and all(v == "done" for v in state["plans"].values())
466	          and all(bool(d) for d in state["decisive"].values()))
467	    return "done" if ok else "failed"

470	def read_new_lines(path: str, offset: int) -> tuple[list[str], int]:
471	    """Read whole journal lines appended since ``offset``; defer a torn tail.
472	
473	    Reads bytes from ``offset`` to EOF, cuts at the last newline, and returns
474	    only the complete lines plus the advanced offset (exactly past that
475	    newline). An incomplete trailing line — the reader racing the workflow's
476	    append (WATCHER-2), possibly truncating a multibyte char (WATCHER-3) — is
477	    left for the next poll: when ``rfind`` finds no newline, nothing is consumed
478	    and the offset does not move. Decoding uses ``errors="replace"`` so a torn
479	    multibyte tail can never crash the process (D5).
480	    """
481	    try:
482	        with open(path, "rb") as f:
483	            f.seek(offset)
484	            chunk = f.read()
485	    except OSError:
486	        return [], offset
487	    cut = chunk.rfind(b"\n")
488	    if cut == -1:
489	        return [], offset
490	    text = chunk[:cut + 1].decode(errors="replace")
491	    return text.splitlines(), offset + cut + 1

497	    ``.watcher-state.json`` records the resolved JOURNAL path. If the stored
498	    journal differs from the current one (auto-discovery or a wf_dir change
499	    picked a different run), the byte offset is meaningless against the new
500	    journal — applying it would skip the new run's head or, if the new journal
501	    is shorter, stall the tailer forever — so reset offset=0 and clear all
502	    derived run state before tailing.
503	    """

505	    try:
506	        with open(STATE) as f:
507	            state = json.load(f)
508	    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
509	        return fresh
510	    if state.get("journal") != JOURNAL:
511	        return fresh
512	    return state

523	def main() -> None:
524	    state = load_state()
525	    state.setdefault("agents", {})
526	    state.setdefault("running", [])
527	    state.setdefault("tok_emitted", {})
528	    state.setdefault("plans", {})
529	    state.setdefault("decisive", {})
530	    state.setdefault("last_plan", None)
531	    state.setdefault("run_complete", None)
532	    for cached in state["agents"].values():  # pre-upgrade cache entries lack "stage"
533	        cached.setdefault("stage", cached.get("role", "work").split(":")[-1])
534	    emit("watcher", "info", "decision watcher online (tailing workflow journal)")
535	    # One-time backfill: token events written before the cache-write split
536	    # carry no "cache_write", so replayed history under-reports w:. Re-read
537	    # every already-tracked agent and emit a quiet delta for whatever the
538	    # emitted totals are missing (normally just the cache-write component).
539	    for aid, prev in list(state["tok_emitted"].items()):
540	        tin, tcached, twrite, tout = agent_tokens(aid)
541	        # Monotonic counters (D7): clamp deltas >= 0; never lower the baseline.
542	        deltas = {"in": max(0, tin - prev.get("in", 0)),
543	                  "out": max(0, tout - prev.get("out", 0)),
544	                  "cached": max(0, tcached - prev.get("cached", 0)),
545	                  "cache_write": max(0, twrite - prev.get("cache_write", 0))}
546	        if not any(deltas.values()):
547	            continue
548	        info = state["agents"].get(aid)
549	        plan = info["plan"] if info else "orchestrator"
550	        label = f"{info['role']} #{info['attempt']}" if info else aid[:8]
551	        new_base = {"in": max(prev.get("in", 0), tin), "out": max(prev.get("out", 0), tout),
552	                    "cached": max(prev.get("cached", 0), tcached),
553	                    "cache_write": max(prev.get("cache_write", 0), twrite)}
554	        emit("tokens", "info", f"{label} token backfill", plan=plan,
555	             extra={"tokens": deltas, "quiet": True,
556	                    # no "state" key: leave the row's queued/running/done dot as-is
557	                    "agent": {"id": aid[:8], "label": label,
558	                              "tokens": {"in": new_base["in"], "out": new_base["out"],
559	                                         "cached": new_base["cached"],
560	                                         "cache_write": new_base["cache_write"]}}})
561	        state["tok_emitted"][aid] = new_base
562	    save_state(state)
563	    tick = 0
564	    quiet_since = None  # wall-clock start of the current terminal-quiet stretch
565	    # False only until the first poll catches up with the journal: a chunk read
566	    # after that was appended within the last poll interval (fresh), while the
567	    # startup chunk may be hours-old backlog whose read time means nothing.
568	    caught_up = False
569	    while True:
570	        try:
571	            size = os.path.getsize(JOURNAL)
572	        except OSError:
573	            time.sleep(1)
574	            continue
575	        if size > state["offset"]:
576	            live = caught_up
577	            lines, new_offset = read_new_lines(JOURNAL, state["offset"])
578	            for line in lines:
579	                line = line.strip()
580	                if not line:
581	                    continue
582	                try:
583	                    entry = json.loads(line)
584	                except json.JSONDecodeError:
585	                    continue
586	                agent_id = entry.get("agentId", "")
587	                if entry.get("type") == "started":
588	                    if state.get("run_complete"):
589	                        # The badge closed (watcher-detected quiet end or the
590	                        # driver's own event) yet the run spawned again: reopen.
591	                        state["run_complete"] = None
592	                        emit("complete", "running", "run resumed: new agent spawned",
593	                             ts=first_ts(agent_id))
594	                    info = classify(agent_id)
595	                    if agent_id not in state["running"]:
596	                        state["running"].append(agent_id)
597	                    if info:
598	                        state["agents"][agent_id] = info
599	                        ts0 = first_ts(agent_id)
600	                        # A sequential loop runs one agent per plan+role at a
601	                        # time, so a same-role spawn at a GREATER attempt while an
602	                        # earlier one never returned a result means that agent is
603	                        # gone (driver killed or restarted mid-flight): close its
604	                        # row so it doesn't tick "running" forever. Best-effort
605	                        # end time = the dead agent's last transcript activity.
606	                        # Guard on attempt strictly increasing (DRIVER-1): a
607	                        # parallel fan-out spawns many agents at the SAME
608	                        # plan+role+attempt — those are live siblings, not
609	                        # retries, and must never stale-close each other.
610	                        for other in list(state["running"]):
611	                            oinfo = state["agents"].get(other)
612	                            if (other == agent_id or not oinfo
613	                                    or oinfo["plan"] != info["plan"]
614	                                    or oinfo["role"] != info["role"]
615	                                    or info["attempt"] <= oinfo["attempt"]):
616	                                continue
617	                            state["running"].remove(other)
618	                            emit(oinfo["stage"], "stale",
619	                                 f"{oinfo['role']} #{oinfo['attempt']} abandoned — no result, "

Use when building or running multi-agent orchestrations that need live per-plan progress, orchestrator decision tracing, and token accounting on a browser dashboard. Provides generic scripts in .claude/shared/monitoring/ plus the integration protocol.
4	---
5	
6	# Orchestrator monitoring
7	
8	Reusable live monitoring for deterministic orchestrator runs. The generic
9	scripts live in `.claude/shared/monitoring/` (stateless, task-agnostic —
10	do not copy or modify them per task). Each orchestration keeps its own state
11	folder under `.claude/local-orchestrators/<task-name>/`.
12	
13	Full reference: `.claude/shared/monitoring/monitoring.md`. Everything is
14	bash + Python 3 stdlib + a browser — no pip installs, works behind egress
15	proxies.
16	
17	## Architecture
18	
19	- `status.sh` — agents append status events at deterministic points
20	- `events.jsonl` — append-only event stream in the task state folder
21	- `monitor_server.py` — serves the dashboard at `/` and streams events over a
22	  websocket at `/ws` (full replay on connect, then live tail;
23	  `?task=<name>` selects the task); `/tasks` lists all discovered task
24	  folders; `/health` probe
25	- `decision_watcher.py` — tails the Workflow run's `journal.jsonl`, emits
26	  orchestrator decision events (spawn / verdict / retry / advance) and
27	  per-agent token accounting (live ~1s deltas for running agents, deduped by
28	  API message id, restart-safe)
29	- `monitor.html` — event-driven dashboard: one card per plan, per-stage chips,
30	  newest-first logs, pulsing token counters; never regenerated for updates
31	
32	## Integration steps for a new orchestration
33	
34	1. Create the task state folder and (optionally) pin config:
35	   ```bash
36	   TASK=/path/to/repo/.claude/local-orchestrators/<task-name>
37	   mkdir -p "$TASK"
38	   # optional orch-config.json: {"wf_dir": "<workflow transcript dir>", "port": 8931}
39	   ```
40	2. Seed one card per sub-plan before launching:
41	   ```bash
42	   export ORCH_STATE_DIR="$TASK"
43	   S=/path/to/repo/.claude/shared/monitoring/status.sh
44	   ORCH_TITLE="Phase 1 — parser" "$S" phase1 plan queued "short description"
45	   ```
46	3. In the orchestrator script, embed the classification marker in every
47	   agent prompt — this is the DETERMINISTIC event source (script-authored
48	   text at a fixed control-flow point, recorded in the Workflow journal;
49	   the watcher raises spawn/result/plan-badge events from it with zero LLM
50	   cooperation):
51	     ```
52	     [monitor] plan=<plan-id> stage=<stage> role=<role> attempt=<n>
53	     ```
54	     `stage=` may be omitted if the prompt mandates a `status.sh ... running`
55	     command naming the stage. The LAST marker occurrence in the prompt wins
56	     (quoted findings/JSON may embed stray markers from earlier agents).
57	     Roles `impl`, `test`, `critique`, `gate:run`, `gate:fix`, `e2e:run`,
58	     `e2e:fix` get semantic decision lines; other roles get generic ones.
59	     Result state derives from the structured-output shape
60	     (`findings`/`real`/`fixed_ids`/`files_changed`/`passed`/`approved`).
61	   Optionally ALSO mandate status calls at fixed points for intra-agent
62	   progress notes — best-effort color, not the source of truth (note:
63	   agents need `ORCH_STATE_DIR` in the command, or a wrapper/symlink in
64	   the state folder):
65	     ```
66	     FIRST run: ORCH_STATE_DIR=<task-dir> bash <shared>/status.sh <plan> <stage> running "attempt N: ..."
67	     LAST  run: ORCH_STATE_DIR=<task-dir> bash <shared>/status.sh <plan> <stage> done|failed "attempt N: <summary>"
68	     ```
69	     Mark plan completion with `... <plan> plan done "..."`.
70	   When the whole run ends, the driver MUST close the Orchestrator card's
71	   badge (the watcher cannot see run completion in the journal — without
72	   this the card shows `running` forever):
73	     ```
74	     ORCH_STATE_DIR=<task-dir> bash <shared>/status.sh orchestrator complete done "<run summary>"
75	     ```
76	4. Start the daemons (background; restart-safe):
77	   ```bash
78	   ORCH_STATE_DIR="$TASK" python3 <shared>/monitor_server.py &   # port: argv > $ORCH_PORT > config > 8931
79	   ORCH_STATE_DIR="$TASK" python3 <shared>/decision_watcher.py & # wf_dir: argv > $ORCH_WF_DIR > config > newest wf_* journal
80	   ```
81	5. Dashboard: `http://<host>:8931/`. If the sandbox's ports aren't reachable
82	   from the host, run `monitor_server.py` on the host — if the state folder is
83	   on a shared mount it tails the same `events.jsonl`. `ORCH_STATE_DIR` is
84	   optional for the daemons: unset, they auto-discover the most recently
85	   active `.claude/local-orchestrators/*/events.jsonl` (both print the
86	   resolved state dir on startup). It stays required in agent `status.sh`
87	   calls, which must never guess where to write. When several orchestrations
88	   run at once, one `monitor_server.py` serves them all — the dashboard's
89	   header dropdown switches tasks live (`/tasks` rescans the folder per
90	   request, so later-started tasks appear without a restart); run one
91	   `decision_watcher.py` per task.
92	
93	## Event schema (one JSON line per event)
94	
95	```json
96	{"ts": "<ISO>", "plan": "<id>", "stage": "<stage>", "state": "queued|running|done|failed|info|stale", "detail": "...", "title": "<optional>", "tokens": {"in": 0, "out": 0, "cached": 0, "cache_write": 0}, "quiet": true}
97	```
98	
99	Reserved: plan id `orchestrator` (wide card, pinned last — the watcher writes
100	there); stage `plan` (sets the card badge); stage `complete` (badge alias of
101	`plan` — for the final run-summary event on the `orchestrator` card); stage
102	`tokens` (delta added to the card's token counter; `quiet` events skip the
103	log). Any event's `title` renames its card. `state: "stale"` marks an abandoned
104	agent/row (watcher-emitted). `tokens` deltas carry optional `cached` (cache-read,
105	shown as `r:`) and `cache_write` (cache-write, shown as `w:`) breakdowns on top
106	of total `in`.
107	
108	The decision watcher also attaches a per-subagent `agent` sub-object that drives
109	the live per-agent rows and the impl→test→critique flow strip:
110	
111	```json
112	{"agent": {"id": "<agent-id>", "label": "<short label>", "state": "running|done|failed|stale", "tokens": {"in": 0, "out": 0, "cached": 0, "cache_write": 0}, "started": "<ISO>", "runtime": "<seconds/human>"}}
113	```
114	
115	## Operational rules
116	
117	- Completed tasks are history — NEVER delete a finished task's state folder
118	  or its `events.jsonl`. The dashboard's task dropdown lists every surviving
119	  folder and full history replays on connect, so a monitor started later
120	  still shows old runs' complete progress. There is no completion cleanup
121	  step.
122	- Resetting a run (wipe-and-rerun of one task still being iterated on — not
123	  cleanup after completion): stop daemons, delete that task's `events.jsonl`
124	  + `.watcher-state.json` from the state folder, re-seed, restart — the
125	  watcher re-backfills the whole journal with true timestamps (spawn = first
126	  transcript line, result = last).
127	- Never `pkill -f` these scripts from a command that spells the script name —
128	  bracket the first letter: `pkill -f "[m]onitor_server"`.
129	- Keep detail strings short, single-line, without double quotes.

5	
6	# execute-research — deterministic research orchestrator
7	
8	Owns the *research → plan* half of a research→implement pair: it emits ONE
9	complete plan that `implement-plan` consumes via a file hand-off and divides
10	itself. Never edits source, never implements, never partitions.
11	
12	**Argument**: `<user_prompt>` — what to research and why (a codebase area, a
13	bug class, a design question, docs/logs/URLs). Everything after an optional
14	`Hints:` marker is `<research_hints>` (files to prioritize, a perspective to
15	emphasize, "then implement it").
16	
17	## Contract (what this skill produces)
18	
19	A plan at `.claude/local-orchestrators/<task-name>/plan/<name>-plan.md` plus a
20	structured return `{ plan_file, item_count, summary }`. The plan is ONE
21	complete, self-contained document — never divided into sub-plans (that
22	divide-and-conquer belongs to `implement-plan`'s Fable divider). It carries:
23	
24	- **global decisions** — every cross-cutting/protocol question decided ONCE so
25	  downstream work cannot diverge;
26	- **ordered implementation items** — per item: id, title, affected files
27	  (file:line), the finding ids it resolves, the decided approach, and what a
28	  test should cover.
29	
30	Findings stay in the research files (the plan references them by id). Keep each
31	item concrete and self-contained enough for `implement-plan` to partition by
32	file ownership without re-research.
33	
34	## Procedure
35	
36	`templates/research.workflow.js` (next to this file) is the NORMATIVE
37	protocol — prompts, schemas, models, monitor markers, status.sh calls, phase
38	structure. Adapt it into
39	`.claude/local-orchestrators/<task-name>/orch-scripts/research.workflow.js`
40	(all task state lives under the task folder), deciding only:
41	
42	1. SUBJECT — the exact files / dirs / sources to study.
43	2. PERSPECTIVES — a deterministic list that partitions the subject (per module
44	   / layer / concern / source); the fan-out and prompts must be a pure function
45	   of it.
46	3. Task name, RESEARCH_CONTEXT, and how `<research_hints>` slot in.
47	
48	Run it, keeping the template's invariants:
49	
50	- Research fan-out is parallel with a barrier (synthesis needs all reports);
51	  synthesis is ONE agent reading all findings files from disk.
52	- All agents are READ-ONLY for source; findings/plan files are task state and
53	  MUST be written. Empirical checks only in a throwaway dir under
54	  `/tmp/claude-1000`; web research may use WebSearch / WebFetch.
55	- Models: research = `opus` (effort by complexity, never above xhigh);
56	  synthesizer = `fable` — the only Fable role here (the others are
57	  `implement-plan`'s divider and final-gate reviewer). Brand-new subagent every
58	  time; never resume / continue / SendMessage a prior one.
59	- Keep the `[monitor] plan=… stage=… role=research|synth attempt=…` markers and
60	  the status.sh calls exactly as templated.
61	
62	## Monitoring
63	
64	Per the `m-orchestrator` skill (scripts in `.claude/shared/monitoring/`) — if
65	that skill does not exist, STOP and notify the caller instead of improvising.
66	Seed one card per phase-stream (`research`, `synthesis`) before launching and
67	start the daemons. When synthesis finishes, the plan card closes via the
68	templated status calls; the driver closes the badge with
69	`status.sh orchestrator complete done "<run summary>"`.
70	
71	## Completion
72	
73	Present the plan's item summary and the plan-file path. Build an HTML final
74	report via the artifact flow: load the `artifact-design` skill FIRST (design
75	guidance), write the page to
76	`.claude/local-orchestrators/<task-name>/report/research-report.html`
77	(named so an auto-chained `implement-plan` run's `final-report.html` cannot
78	overwrite it), then publish that file with the Artifact tool. The task-folder
79	file is the required local copy — the dashboard auto-links artifacts inside
80	the task folder, so it must live there, not in /tmp, and stays even after
81	publishing. KEEP the task state folder (including `events.jsonl`) — completed
82	runs are monitor history; never delete or truncate.
83	
84	**Auto-chain**: only if `<user_prompt>` / `<research_hints>` asks to implement
85	/ build / execute it — then invoke the `implement-plan` skill on the SAME task
86	folder, handing `{ plan_file }` only (its Fable divider derives the sub-plans;
87	sequential default). Otherwise hand off the plan and stop.

30	`.claude/local-orchestrators/<task-name>/orch-scripts/implement.workflow.js`,
31	invoked with `args = { plan_file, parallel }` (all task state lives under the
32	task folder), deciding only:
33	
34	1. Task name, REPO/TASK paths, TASK_SPECIFIC_CONTEXT.
35	2. TARGETED_TEST_COMMAND / FULL_SUITE_COMMAND / BASELINE_NOTES, folding in

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stdlib-only tests for monitor_server.py (run: python3 test_server.py).

No pytest, no omnigent imports. Uses an ephemeral throwaway state dir under
/tmp/claude-1000 and never touches the live monitor's events.jsonl. Asserts fail
loudly (AssertionError -> non-zero exit).
"""
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
MODULE_PATH = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "monitor_server.py"))

# Resolve STATE_DIR/PORT at import to a throwaway dir so nothing touches the
# live task folder. No server is started (main() is never called).
_TMP_BASE = os.environ.get("TMPDIR") or "/tmp/claude-1000"
os.makedirs(_TMP_BASE, exist_ok=True)
_STATE_DIR = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="srvtest-", dir=_TMP_BASE)
os.environ["ORCH_STATE_DIR"] = _STATE_DIR
os.environ.pop("ORCH_PORT", None)


def _load_module():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("monitor_server_undertest", MODULE_PATH)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod


ms = _load_module()


def test_read_frames_torn_line():
    """A torn trailing line is deferred, never dropped (SERVER-1 / D5)."""
    path = os.path.join(_STATE_DIR, "torn.jsonl")
    a = json.dumps({"ts": "a", "plan": "p1"})
    b = json.dumps({"ts": "b", "plan": "p2"})
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write((a + "\n" + b + "\n").encode())
        f.write(b'{"ts":"c","pla')  # partial, no newline
    frames, off = ms.read_frames(path, 0)
    assert frames == [a.encode(), b.encode()], frames
    # offset must stop before the partial line
    assert off == len((a + "\n" + b + "\n").encode()), off
    # complete the torn line + append another record
    c = json.dumps({"ts": "c", "plan": "p3"})
    d = json.dumps({"ts": "d", "plan": "p4"})
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write((a + "\n" + b + "\n" + c + "\n" + d + "\n").encode())
    frames2, off2 = ms.read_frames(path, off)
    # the middle event c must reappear intact, never lost
    assert frames2 == [c.encode(), d.encode()], frames2
    assert off2 == len((a + "\n" + b + "\n" + c + "\n" + d + "\n").encode()), off2

# Research findings — perspective: PRIOR ART (`.claude/shared/monitoring/` + the three skills)

Read the implementation, not the docs. Every claim below is anchored to a line
or to a command whose output I inspected. Empirical checks were run in
`/tmp/claude-1000/priorart/`; the live task folder was only read, never written
(except the two mandated `status.sh` calls).

## What the module already gets RIGHT (reuse verbatim — see PRIORART-18)

Before the defects: this is a genuinely well-built prototype. Torn-tail
tailing, checkpoint-with-identity, monotonic token deltas, message-id dedup,
session-id rotation survival, realpath containment and escape-first rendering
are all correct and tested. The findings below are about **scope**, not craft.

---

## PRIORART-1 — The transport is one-directional by construction; there is no place to put a control command

**File**: `.claude/shared/monitoring/monitor_server.py:393-514` (`handle`),
`:313-327` (`drain_client`), `:358-388` (`stream_events`)
**Severity**: blocker

**Scenario.** Touch's per-terminal page must "pause, restart, start and
terminate agent loops" (README.md:5-6) and the main page must accept keystrokes
into a live Claude Code session (README.md:3-4). Nothing in the prior art can
carry a byte from browser to backend:

- `handle()` parses the request line at `:403-404` but **never reads the HTTP
  method** and never reads a request body (it stops at `readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")`,
  `:397`). A `POST /control` is indistinguishable from `GET /control`.
- The websocket is server→client only: `drain_client()` (`:313-327`) exists
  purely to *discard* client frames and detect CLOSE. `parse_client_frames()`
  (`:279-310`) deliberately skips over payloads without ever decoding them —
  it does not even unmask.
- Every route that is not `/ws`, `/health`, `/tasks`, `/artifacts`, `/file`
  falls through to the catch-all that returns `monitor.html` with **200**
  (`:495-506`).

The data model has the same shape: `events.jsonl` is append-only and every
consumer (`read_frames`, `task_status`, the browser) is a pure reader.

**Recommendation.** Do not "add a POST endpoint" to `monitor_server.py` — its
request loop has no method dispatch, no body reader, no routing table, and no
keep-alive (every response hard-codes `Connection: close`). Keep the *reader*
half (tail + replay + WS framing) as a component, and put commands on a
separate, explicitly-designed plane. Migration consequence: the reader half is
~120 lines of `monitor_server.py` (`ws_frame`, `parse_client_frames`,
`drain_client`, `read_frames`, `stream_events`) and lifts cleanly; the
`handle()` router does not and should be replaced.

---

## PRIORART-2 — Zero authentication, no Origin check, no Host check, binds 0.0.0.0 — safe for a read-only dashboard, fatal the moment controls exist

**File**: `monitor_server.py:519` (`asyncio.start_server(handle, "0.0.0.0", PORT)`),
`:412-441` (the entire `/ws` admission check)
**Severity**: blocker

**Scenario.** The `/ws` upgrade validates exactly two things:
`sec-websocket-key` present and `sec-websocket-version in (None, "13")`. There
is no `Origin` validation, no `Host` allowlist, no token, no cookie, no
same-origin requirement. WebSocket connections are **not** subject to CORS, so
any web page the user visits in the same browser can today do
`new WebSocket("ws://<sandbox-host>:8931/ws?task=<name>")` and read the entire
event stream, and `fetch("/file?task=…&path=…")` to read every `.md`/`.html`
under a task folder (opaque-response restrictions do not apply to the WS path).
A `Host:`-header-based DNS-rebinding attack is likewise unblocked.

Today the blast radius is "an attacker learns your agent logs". Once the same
origin accepts *pause/terminate/start* commands and terminal keystrokes, the
blast radius becomes **arbitrary command execution in the user's repo**, and it
is reachable by CSRF from any tab. The environment makes this worse, not
better: the module is documented to bind `0.0.0.0` and be published to the host
(`CLAUDE.md:112-114`).

**Recommendation.** Decide the auth model **before** writing the first write
endpoint, not after: a per-boot random token in the URL (`/?k=<token>`) that the
page echoes into the WS query + an `Origin`/`Host` allowlist enforced in the
upgrade handler is the minimum, and is ~20 lines. Migration consequence: the
token must be printed on stdout at startup (the module already prints its state
dir at `:523-525`, so the pattern exists) and every `sbx ports --publish`
instruction in the docs must carry it.

---

## PRIORART-3 — The unit of aggregation is a repo-local task folder, not a Claude Code session

**File**: `monitor_server.py:21` (`TASKS_ROOT = .../local-orchestrators`),
`:49-62` (`discover_tasks`), `:148-151` (`resolve_task_dir`)
**Severity**: major

**Scenario.** Touch's sidebar is "a list of such terminal sessions"
(README.md:4). The prior art's list is `.claude/local-orchestrators/*/`
directories in **one repo**, discovered by `os.listdir` of a path computed
relative to the module's own location (`:21`). It never opens `~/.claude` at
all except in the watcher's journal auto-discovery.

Ground truth for what Touch actually needs is elsewhere and is richer.
`~/.claude/sessions/622.json` contains:

```json
{"pid":622,"sessionId":"dd469822-…","cwd":"/home/laniakea/Projects/touch",
 "startedAt":1784946693282,"procStart":"10028","version":"2.1.220",
 "peerProtocol":1,"kind":"interactive","entrypoint":"cli","name":"touch-2b",
 "nameSource":"derived","status":"busy","updatedAt":…,"statusUpdatedAt":…}
```

and the CLI binary reads additional per-session fields `tempo`
(`active|idle|blocked`), `needs`, and `tmux` from those same files (verified:
`grep -aoP '.{0,120}peerProtocol.{0,220}' /home/agent/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.220`).
That is exactly the sidebar model — with a live status, a name, a cwd and a pid
— and the prior art has no concept of any of it. Note also that
`local-orchestrators/*/` in this repo is **carried-over history from a
different project** (`CLAUDE.md:127-130`), so its own discovery root is not
even describing this machine's runs.

**Recommendation.** Build session discovery as a new layer over
`~/.claude/sessions/*.json` + `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<sessionId>.jsonl`, and
demote `events.jsonl` to a *per-run overlay* joined onto a session by id. Reuse
the shape of `tasks_payload()` (`:133-145`) — name/mtime/status/last/tokens per
entry is the right tile payload — but not its source. Migration consequence:
`?task=<name>` becomes `?session=<uuid>` (+ optionally `&run=<wfId>`), which
breaks every saved dashboard URL; do it now while there are none.

---

## PRIORART-4 — Only Workflow-tool agents carrying the `[monitor]` marker are visible; ordinary session subagents are invisible

**File**: `decision_watcher.py:115-135` (`MARKER`, `STAGE_HINT`,
`ROLE_PATTERNS`), `:330-367` (`classify`), `:53-73` (journal pinning)
**Severity**: major

**Scenario.** The watcher's only input is one `wf_*/journal.jsonl`, and an
agent only becomes anything but "unclassified" (`:664-666`) if the first line of
its transcript contains
`[monitor] plan=… role=… attempt=…`. That marker is authored by the
orchestrator workflow script — so the watcher sees **only** agents spawned by
an `execute-research`/`implement-plan` workflow.

But a Claude Code session spawns subagents outside workflows too, and they are
recorded in a completely different place with a completely different shape.
Verified in this very session:

```
~/.claude/projects/-home-laniakea-Projects-touch/<sessionId>/subagents/
  agent-a4e343a0f7d73268c.jsonl        (937 KB)
  agent-a4e343a0f7d73268c.meta.json -> {"agentType":"general-purpose",
      "description":"Assess control and UI feasibility",
      "toolUseId":"toolu_017UzEDnR28ARKERuMw2PGwX","spawnDepth":1,"model":"opus"}
  agent-a483cae616edffe81.jsonl        (421 KB)
```

Two real subagents, no journal, no marker, `spawnDepth` and `toolUseId` instead
— and the workflow variant's meta is *poorer*
(`{"agentType":"workflow-subagent","spawnDepth":1,"model":"opus"}`, no
description, no toolUseId). README.md:1 says Touch visualizes "subagents in a
Claude Code session"; the prior art can see roughly half of them, and the half
it can see is the half that needed a special prompt convention.

**Recommendation.** Make the **session transcript** the primary source: the
`Task` tool_use/tool_result pairs in `<sessionId>.jsonl` give you parent→child
edges, labels (`description`), and the `toolUseId` join key to
`subagents/agent-*.meta.json`, with zero prompt cooperation. Keep the
`[monitor]` marker as *optional enrichment* that adds plan/stage/attempt
semantics when a workflow authored it. Migration consequence: `classify()` stops
being the gate on visibility and becomes a decorator — the marker convention
survives, but nothing depends on it any more.

---

## PRIORART-5 — Parallel fan-out is unrepresentable: six live agents render as six identical rows and collapse into ONE graph node

**File**: `decision_watcher.py:636-638` and `:682-688` (label construction),
`monitor.html:287-293` (`upsertAgent` role derivation), `:300-321` (`renderFlow`)
**Proof**: `.claude/local-orchestrators/touch-aggregator/events.jsonl:12,15,17,19,21,23`
**Severity**: major

**Scenario.** The watcher builds every agent label as
`f"{info['role']} #{info['attempt']}"` — role and attempt only. It **has**
`info["stage"]` in hand (it uses it as the emitted event's stage on the very
same line) and throws it away. For a `parallel()` fan-out every sibling shares
role and attempt, so every label is identical. From the live run right now:

```
events.jsonl:12  "stage":"sessiondata" … "agent":{"id":"a2fc883c","label":"research #1"…}
events.jsonl:15  "stage":"liveio"      … "agent":{"id":"a74f0c93","label":"research #1"…}
events.jsonl:17  "stage":"control"     … "agent":{"id":"a9eabf26","label":"research #1"…}
events.jsonl:19  "stage":"agentgraph"  … "agent":{"id":"a82d2e25","label":"research #1"…}
events.jsonl:21  "stage":"stack"       … "agent":{"id":"a79fa2f4","label":"research #1"…}
events.jsonl:23  "stage":"priorart"    … "agent":{"id":"a2ec1069","label":"research #1"…}
```

The frontend renders `a.label || a.id` into `.alabel` (`monitor.html:278`) and
never shows the id, so the user sees six rows all reading `research #1`. Worse,
the flow strip derives its node key by `(a.label||a.id).split(" #")[0]`
(`:287`) → all six map to the single role `"research"` → `renderFlow` draws
**one** node. The orchestrator log is equally degenerate: six consecutive
identical `"spawn research research attempt 1"` lines (`events.jsonl:11,14,16,
18,20,22`).

This is precisely the case Touch's n8n-style graph exists to show.

**Recommendation.** Two-line fix in the watcher: label as
`f"{info['stage']}:{info['role']} #{info['attempt']}"`, and add explicit
`agent.stage` / `agent.role` / `agent.attempt` fields to the `agent` sub-object
rather than making the UI reverse-engineer them out of a display string.
Migration consequence: purely additive to the event schema — already-recorded
history (which the ops rules forbid deleting, `CLAUDE.md:118-121`) still renders,
just with the old collapsed labels.

---

## PRIORART-6 — The event schema is a flat state overlay; it cannot express a graph, and it has no version field

**File**: `.claude/shared/monitoring/monitoring.md:25-46` (normative schema),
`monitor.html:203-219` (`planEl` — one card per `plan` id)
**Severity**: major

**Scenario.** The whole model is `(plan, stage, state)` → one card per `plan`,
one chip per `stage`, plus a per-agent row list. There are **no node ids, no
edges, no parent/child, no ordering other than first-seen**. `renderFlow`
(`monitor.html:300-321`) fakes a topology by iterating `p.roles` in insertion
order and drawing `→` between consecutive entries — that is a rendering
accident, not data. An n8n-like UML graph needs an actual node/edge structure
(fan-out, barrier/join, retry back-edge, gate branch), and none of it can be
derived from this stream.

Separately: events carry **no schema version**. Backward compatibility so far
has been achieved by defaulting missing keys (`ev.tokens.cached || 0`,
`monitor.html:371`; the one-time backfill at `decision_watcher.py:538-561`).
Any *structural* change is unabsorbable, and the operating rule is that
completed runs' `events.jsonl` are permanent history that replays on connect
(`monitoring.md:183-187`).

**Recommendation.** (a) Derive the graph topology from a source that actually
has one — the workflow script's phase/`agent()` structure plus the journal's
spawn order and the session transcript's Task parent/child edges — and use
events only to *paint state onto* nodes. (b) Add `"v": 2` to every emitted
event now, and have readers treat a missing `v` as 1. Migration consequence:
one field in `emit()` (`decision_watcher.py:138-152`) and in `status.sh:34-40`;
doing it later means either a lossy history migration or a permanent branch in
the reader.

---

## PRIORART-7 — The watcher fully re-parses every running agent's entire transcript once per second (O(size) per tick, and size grows all run)

**File**: `decision_watcher.py:154-197` (`agent_tokens`), `:86-100`
(`agent_paths`), called from `:764-795` (every ~1s) and `:678`, `:705`
**Severity**: major

**Scenario.** `agent_tokens(aid)` globs
`~/.claude/projects/*/*/subagents/workflows/<wf>/agent-<id>.jsonl` (a filesystem
glob, per agent, per tick) and then reads and `json.loads`-es **every line of
every copy** to rebuild `usage_by_msg` from scratch. It is called for every
still-running agent on every 1-second poll, and again on every result.

Measured on the live run (`/tmp/claude-1000/priorart/bench.py`):

```
6 transcripts, 2.26 MB, 456 usage rows, one full pass = 16 ms   [6 minutes in]
```

16 ms/s is nothing — but the cost is linear in transcript size, which grows for
the whole run. Extrapolating from the measured rate (~0.38 MB per agent per
6 min), a 2-hour six-agent implement loop reaches ~45 MB, i.e. **~300+ ms of
JSON parsing every single second**, on the *same single thread* that tails the
journal, classifies spawns, and runs the completion debounce. Touch wants to
watch whole sessions, whose transcripts are larger still (this session's
`<sessionId>.jsonl` is 777 KB after ~30 minutes).

**Recommendation.** Apply the module's own checkpoint pattern one level down:
store `{path: (byte_offset, partial_usage_totals)}` per transcript in
`.watcher-state.json` and only parse the appended tail — `read_new_lines()`
(`:470-491`) is already exactly the right primitive and is already tested.
Message-id dedup still works because you keep the accumulated id set (or, since
ids are per-message and monotonic, just the running sums plus a small
recently-seen id window). Migration consequence: `.watcher-state.json` gains a
key; `load_state()`'s journal-identity reset (`:494-512`) already handles a
stale/incompatible checkpoint by discarding it.

---

## PRIORART-8 — Full replay from byte 0 on every connect, one WS frame per event, no log trimming — and the UI offers a 500 ms full-resync button

**File**: `monitor_server.py:358-378` (`stream_events`, `offset = 0`, one
`writer.write(ws_frame(line))` per line), `monitor.html:699-708` (clear + rebuild
on every `onopen`), `:390-391` (unbounded `log.insertBefore` + `render()` on
every event), `:172-181` and `:714-732` (`rateSel` / `forceResync`)
**Severity**: major

**Scenario.** There is no resume cursor: every `/ws` connection replays the file
from offset 0 as individual text frames, and the page throws away all DOM and
accumulators and rebuilds. Then:

- `render()` runs on **every** event and re-`appendChild`s **every** card
  (`monitor.html:220-238`) — O(events × plans) DOM moves during replay.
- log `<li>`s are never trimmed (`:390`), so replay materialises one DOM node
  per historical event.
- the refresh dropdown offers **500 ms**, and `forceResync()` implements it by
  *closing and reopening the socket* (`:717-724`) — i.e. a full history replay
  twice per second.

Measured on the live run: **375 events / 150 871 bytes in ~6 minutes** for a
single six-agent research phase — ~1.5 MB/h, dominated by the quiet 1 Hz token
ticks (`decision_watcher.py:781-791`). One hour of history on the 500 ms setting
is ≈3 MB/s of replay per open tab, and ≈21 600 log DOM nodes. Touch's terminal
view (which must replay a session transcript, already 777 KB at 30 min) makes
this the dominant cost of the whole product.

**Recommendation.** Add `?from=<byte-offset>` (or `?after=<seq>`) to `/ws`,
batch replay into multi-line frames, emit an explicit `{"kind":"replay-end"}`
marker, cap the client log with a ring buffer, and coalesce `render()` into a
`requestAnimationFrame`. Migration consequence: the client must persist a
cursor and keep its accumulators across reconnects — which means giving up the
"full replay is safe against double counting" invariant that the current design
leans on (`monitoring.md:172-175`); the replacement invariant is
"events are ordered and idempotent by seq", which is stronger and is what a
control plane needs anyway.

---

## PRIORART-9 — The watcher is structurally blind to control actions, so a paused/stopped run will be reported as a completed one

**File**: `decision_watcher.py:110-113` (`QUIET_SECS`), `:450-467`
(`run_outcome`), `:731-762` (the completion sweep)
**Proof**: `grep -aoP 'resumeFromRunId.{0,400}' /home/agent/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.220`
**Severity**: major

**Scenario.** Verified against the CLI binary: a Workflow run is a background
task in a task registry — the binary contains
`i.type==="local_workflow" && i.status==="running" && i.workflowRunId===e.resumeFromRunId`
and the user-facing string *"Workflow ${runId} is still running (task ${id}).
Stop it first with TaskStop({taskId: …}) before resuming."* And, decisively:

> *"It may have been stopped (via the UI or TaskStop — **these leave no
> transcript marker**), or it may have been running when the previous Claude
> Code process exited."*

So a stopped workflow and a stalled workflow produce **byte-identical**
journals. The watcher's only terminal signal is the 60-second quiet debounce
(`:738-760`), which will confidently emit
`orchestrator complete done|failed … "(watcher-detected end)"` and settle every
open plan card by `state["decisive"]` (`:748-753`) — i.e. it will fabricate a
verdict for a run the user *paused on purpose*, and the fabricated verdict will
usually be `failed` (because `decisive` is unset for a plan mid-loop, `:751`).

**Recommendation.** Once Touch owns the control actions it must record them
itself (an append-only control log: `paused|resumed|stopped|started`, with
runId, taskId and actor) and *join* that onto the derived state, with the
control log winning. Concretely: gate the quiet-debounce close behind "no
pause/stop recorded for this run". Migration consequence: `run_outcome()` grows
an input it currently cannot see; the 60 s heuristic stays only as the fallback
for runs Touch did not initiate.

---

## PRIORART-10 — "Restart" is `resumeFromRunId` cache replay into a NEW journal, and the checkpoint model turns that into duplicated history

**File**: `decision_watcher.py:494-512` (`load_state` journal-identity reset),
`:72-74` (`JOURNAL`/`WF_NAME` fixed at import)
**Proof**: binary text *"To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch
with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of
agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and
everything after it runs live."*
**Severity**: major

**Scenario.** The harness's restart primitive replays cached `agent()` results
into a **new run**, with a new runId and (per `nEp()` in the binary, which
symlinks a canonical `workflowRunId` path at the `transcriptDir`) a new
transcript dir and journal. `load_state()` sees `state["journal"] != JOURNAL`
and — correctly, for its own assumptions — resets `offset=0` and discards all
derived state. The watcher then re-emits the *entire* spawn/result/token history
of the resumed run into the **same** `events.jsonl`, on top of the original
run's events. The dashboard replays both: duplicate agent rows (different agent
ids), duplicated token deltas on the card counters (`monitor.html:370-372`
accumulates unconditionally), and a card whose badge flips through two runs'
worth of transitions.

Note the harness *does* hand you the dedup key and the prior art ignores it —
every journal `started` line carries a content hash:

```
{"type":"started","key":"v2:c13a866b3bd1e7129557fc996a218a044553d0115ac84c64a6184c41e4042639","agentId":"a2fc883c96ff7b837"}
```

(verified: `~/.claude/projects/…/subagents/workflows/wf_829e6f58-b2f/journal.jsonl`).
`key` is stable across a cached resume; `agentId` is not. The watcher reads only
`type` and `agentId` (`:586-587`).

**Recommendation.** Key run state by `(runId, key)` rather than by journal path
+ agentId: a `started` whose `key` was already emitted is a cache replay and
must update the existing node, not create a second one. Migration consequence:
`.watcher-state.json` gains a `keys` map and `load_state`'s hard reset becomes a
merge; this is the single change that makes the README's "restart" control
truthful rather than duplicative.

---

## PRIORART-11 — One watcher process per run, with all run identity in module-level globals — the module cannot grow to N sessions

**File**: `decision_watcher.py:19-113` (module-level `ROOT`, `STATE_DIR`,
`WF_DIR`, `JOURNAL`, `WF_NAME`, `EVENTS`, `STATE`, `MAX_*`, `QUIET_SECS` all
resolved at import), `:523-796` (`main()` = one infinite loop over one journal);
`monitoring.md:143-145` ("`decision_watcher.py` still watches one task per
process — start one per concurrent orchestration")
**Severity**: major

**Scenario.** Everything that identifies *which run* is being watched is a
module global computed at import time. Two runs = two OS processes, started by
hand, with no supervisor, no restart, no health check, and nothing that notices
a new run appearing. Touch's sidebar implies N sessions × M runs, discovered
and attached **live**. The server half already solved the multiplicity problem
(one `monitor_server.py` serves every task, rescanning per request,
`:49-62`); the watcher half did not.

**Recommendation.** Refactor the watcher into a `RunWatcher` class holding what
are now globals, plus a supervisor loop that reconciles a watch-set against
disk (new `wf_*/journal.jsonl` appears → attach; journal quiet + run closed →
detach). Migration consequence: this is a real refactor of ~800 lines, not a
wrapper — every helper (`agent_paths`, `agent_tokens`, `prompt_text`,
`first_ts`, `last_ts`, `emit`, `classify`) closes over `WF_DIR`/`WF_NAME`/
`EVENTS` today. Budget it explicitly; the alternative (spawning a process per
run from Touch) inherits a process-lifecycle problem the prior art never had to
solve.

---

## PRIORART-12 — An unknown `?task=` silently streams a different task's data

**File**: `monitor_server.py:148-151` (`discover_tasks().get(task, STATE_DIR)`),
used by `/ws` (`:446`), `/artifacts` (`:457`) and `/file` (`:467`)
**Severity**: minor

**Scenario.** A renamed, deleted, or mistyped task name does not 404 — it
resolves to the process's startup `STATE_DIR` and the client gets a **200/101
with someone else's events, artifacts and files**. The frontend has a
band-aid for the display side (`selectTask` injects a disabled
`"(unknown task)"` option, `monitor.html:598-613`) but the socket is still
streaming the wrong run underneath it: URL, breadcrumb and dropdown say one
thing, the cards show another.

For Touch, where the identifier is a session and the page carries controls,
"silently act on a different target" graduates from confusing to dangerous.

**Recommendation.** Return 404 for an unresolvable id on `/ws`, `/artifacts` and
`/file`; keep the default-selection behaviour only for the *absent* parameter.
Migration consequence: `monitor.html`'s `route()` must handle a failed WS
upgrade as "unknown session" rather than as a retry loop (`:707-708` currently
reconnects forever).

---

## PRIORART-13 — Catch-all route returns the dashboard with 200 for every unknown path; HTTP method is never parsed

**File**: `monitor_server.py:403-404` (request line parsed for path only),
`:495-506` (catch-all)
**Severity**: minor

**Scenario.** `GET /favicon.ico`, `GET /api/anything`, `DELETE /file` all return
the full `monitor.html` body with `200 OK` and `Content-Type: text/html`. There
is no 404, no 405, no method dispatch, and no `HEAD` handling. A browser
requesting `/favicon.ico` downloads the whole dashboard.

(five routes); painful once Touch has thirty.

## PRIORART-14 — `events.jsonl` is multi-writer and its safety rests on an undocumented "one `write()` per record" invariant

**File**: `status.sh:28-45` (`python3 … >> "$STATE_DIR/events.jsonl"`),
`decision_watcher.py:150-151` (`open(EVENTS,"a")` + one `f.write(line+"\n")`)
**Proof**: `/tmp/claude-1000/priorart/interleave.py` and `interleave2.py`
**Severity**: minor (today) / blocker (if Touch reuses the file as a transport)

**Scenario.** N concurrent agents' `status.sh` calls plus the watcher all append
to the same file with no locking. I tested this directly with 4 concurrent
writers × 200 records of ~6 KB each:

```
one write() per record   -> lines=800  corrupted(mixed-writer)=0
record split over 2 write() calls -> lines=800  corrupted(mixed-writer)=206
```

So the current design is genuinely safe — Linux serialises a single `O_APPEND`
`write()` on a regular file — but *only* because every writer today happens to
emit a whole record in exactly one syscall (`print()` on a buffered stdout that
is flushed once at process exit; a single `f.write()`). Nothing documents this,
nothing tests it, and it is exactly the invariant a new writer breaks: a Node.js
`stream.write()` of a large payload, an incrementally-built line, or anything
streaming terminal output in chunks produces the 206/800 case.

**Recommendation.** Write the invariant down next to the schema in
`monitoring.md`, and add it to `test_shell.py` as a concurrency test (it is a
20-line stdlib test). For Touch: do **not** carry terminal I/O over a shared
append-only file — use one file per writer, or a socket. Migration consequence:
none for the existing event stream; it decides Touch's terminal transport.
